The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300­0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to offer public comment from home:
  1. Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until 3:00
  p.m. the day of the meeting, to be read by the City Clerk during public comment.
  Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time, and previously
  distributed public comment will be noted. Any comments received after 3:00 p.m. will
  be included in the public comment record but will not be read at the meeting.
  2. Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
  during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in­person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At this
time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda. Pursuant
to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the meeting
agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place limits on
duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First
Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require
having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or resolution
be read in its entirety before taking any action.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

1.  CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE NO. O­23­1401 (FIRST READING)
  AMENDING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.03.10 TO EXTEND THE
  APPLICABILITY OF OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS TO ALL
  MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL PROJECTS IN THE C­1 ZONE
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council waive full reading of the
  ordinance and introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No. O­23­1401. If
  the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, the appropriate motion would be:“I
  move to waive full reading and introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No.
  O­23­1401 an Ordinance of the City of San Marino Amending San Marino Municipal
  Code Section 23.03.10 to extend the applicability of objective design standards to all
  multifamily residential project in the C­1 zone.”

2.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­05 ADOPTING THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROJECT FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023­24
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct a public hearing to
  consider the use of CDBG funds for the Senior Outreach Program and ADA compliant
  sidewalk replacement program in FY 2023­24. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, the appropriate motion, after the hearing, would be: “I move to
  adopt Resolution No. R­23­05, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of San
  Marino, California adopting the projected use of funds from the Community
  Development Block Grant program for Fiscal Year 2023­24.”

  NEW BUSINESS

3.  APPROVAL OF MODIFICATION TO THE LACY PARK ENTRY/EXIT
  GATES USING DONATION FUNDS
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the modification of the
  Lacy Park entry/exit gates in the amount of $6,245 using donation funds. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to approve the modification of the Lacy Park entry/exit gates as proposed;
  authorize the procurement in the amount of $6,245; appropriate $6,245 to Account
  #281­50­4600­7041 (Lacy Park Gates); and amending Account 281­50­3601­0000
  (Lacy Park Donations Received) by $6,245 for the donation from the San Marino
  Motor Classic.”

4.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION TO ESTABLISH FISCAL YEAR 2023­24
  PUBLIC SAFETY SPECIAL TAX LEVIES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve a public safety
  parcel tax levy of $3,596,800. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:“I move to approve Resolution No.
  R­23­07 establishing the Public Safety Special Tax Levies for Fiscal Year 2023­24.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR
  FEBRUARY 2023
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of February 2023. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to receive and
  file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of February 2023.”

6.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF JANUARY
  2023
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I
  move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of January
  2023.”

7.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the February 2023 minutes.
  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be: “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of February 8, 2023, the
  regular meeting of February 8, 2023, the joint special meeting with the Planning
  Commission of February 24, 2023, the adjourned regular meeting of February 24,
  2023, and the special meeting of February 24, 2023.”

8.  UPDATE ON CITY RESPONSE TO THE COVID­19 PANDEMIC

  City Council concurs with the staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the

  be: “I move to receive and file the March 8, 2023 report on the City’s response to

9.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R­23­06 TO TRANSFER FY 2023­
  24 CDBG PROJECT FUNDS AND PRIOR FISCAL YEARS
  UNALLOCATED FUNDS TO THE CDBG REVOLVING GRANT FUND
  Recommendation: Subject to the approval of the City Council adopting Resolution No.
  R­23­05 to adopt the CDBG project(s) for FY 2023­24 on March 8, 2023, staff
  recommends the City Council adopt the resolution allowing for the City to transfer
  $165,400 of the FY 2023­24 CDBG allocation and prior years’ unallocated CDBG funds
  to the CDBG revolving grant fund. If the Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, the appropriate motion would be: “I move to adopt Resolution No.
  R­23­06 authorizing the transfer of the City’s CDBG funds for Fiscal Year 2023­24 and
  prior fiscal years’ unallocated CDBG funds, totaling $165,400, to the CDBG revolving
  grant fund.”

10.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO TRANSPORTATION
  REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT WITH SAN MARINO UNIFIED
  SCHOOL DISTRICT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council authorize the Acting City
  Manager to execute an amendment to the original transportation reimbursement
  agreement with the District for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024 for
  transportation reimbursements under the terms described in the attached
  agreements. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be: “I move to authorize the Acting City Manager to execute an
  amendment to the original transportation reimbursement agreement with the San
  Marino Unified School District for transportation reimbursements for the year ended
  June 30, 2024.”

11.  AWARD OF 3­YEAR AGREEMENT FOR 4TH OF JULY FIREWORKS
  SHOW TO PYRO SPECTACULARS, INC. WITH A CONTRACT AMOUNT
  OF $109,230
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council award the three­year agreement for
  the 4th of July fireworks show to Pyro Spectaculars, Inc. If the City Council concurs
  with Staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to award the
  three­year agreement for the 4th of July fireworks show to Pyro Spectaculars, Inc,
  and authorize the Acting City Manager to execute the agreement.”

12.  ACCEPTANCE OF $4,518 DONATION FROM THE MACFARLAND
  FAMILY FOUNDATION
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council accept the $4,518 donation from
  the Macfarland Family Foundation. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be: “I move to accept the donation of
  $4,518 from the Macfarland Family Foundation.”

13.  APPROVAL OF A REQUEST FOR THE WAIVING OF ENTRANCE FEES
  AND OPENING LACY PARK EARLY ON APRIL 17, 2022, FOR SAN
  MARINO COMMUNITY CHURCH SUNRISE SERVICE SPECIAL EVENT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council review the Special Event
  Permit Application from the San Marino Community Church for the Sunday Easter
  Sunrise Service event and waive entry fees to Lacy Park and staff fees associated
  with the event. If the City Council deems the application satisfactory, an appropriate
  motion would be: “I move to waive entry fees to Lacy Park associated with the San
  Marino Community Church Sunday Easter Sunrise Service event.”

14.  APPROVAL OF $18,980 BUDGET AMENDMENT TO THE CAPITALIZED
  EQUIPMENT ACCOUNT FOR THE PURCHASE OF GYM EQUIPMENT
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve a budget amendment and
  appropriation of $18,980 from the Capital Equipment Fund reserves to account 591­
  53­4613­0563 (Gym Equipment). If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation,
  an appropriate motion would be: “I move to approve a budget amendment and
  appropriation of $18,980 from the Capital Equipment Fund reserves to account 591­
  53­4613­0563 (Gym Equipment).”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
